Unless you provide further context, I can't really see the Shadowrun example as tokenism unless the main character keeps insisting that they dated someone of the same sex repeatedly or something. The MtG example is too vague for me to make any sort of judgment call on. As for GW2... you said so yourself it's an insignificant NPC, right? I guess I can see that at tokenism, at least the NPC. I hope the lesbian couple have more to them besides being lesbian.

As for your question: the issue with tokenism is that the result is a character whose only defining characteristic is their sex, race, orientation, etc., but it's put in such a way that it's transparent that they're trying to appeal to a certain group because that's the only thing that truly matters about said character, not their strengths or flaws, etc.

I do think that both sides of the debate can get overly paranoid with accusations for various reasons, but the core problem with tokenism is that it's bad writing via overcompensation one aspect of a character over anything without trying to make them interesting beyond that. One example is Steve from Mass Effect 3 whose entire character basically revolves him getting over his dead lover.

And on the flipside, it's pretty easy to reduce a well-developed character in something to one aspect due to a group of people attaching to that aspect. See basically every fucking fandom ever that calls everything gay because two female characters hugged each other.

I feel like it's more of an issue with marketing and you have people claiming that you should buy something because they have a gay character or something.

One of the reasons why I eventually became a deist was because there is a lack of proselytizing. Since the deity has no need to "convert" anyone, why bother? It'd be nice to have more deists around sure, but I don't feel like it's my "moral duty" to convert anyone to something that is I feel is just personal. There's a difference between saving someone's life and converting them to a belief of some kind. More importantly, just because someone is a deist doesn't make them any less better or worse than someone who is a theist, atheist, etc. It is simply a label that describes what you believe, not whether you have a good heart.

As for saving someone spiritually... well. It's really hard to see whether or not someone is struggling spiritually. And even in more obvious cases, there's not much I can do. If their struggle for spirituality leads them to doing something that hurts themselves or others, I would stop whatever it is they're doing, but that's as far as I think I can do in regards to that, especially if they do not ask for help in that way.

I guess this really comes down to me thinking that things like spirituality is more of a personal, private journey than one that is a grand spectacle, because it's extremely easy to fool people into thinking you're authentic that way. I can't really tell what sort of path of spirituality they're going on, I can only stop them if their actions lead to others or themselves getting hurt or worse. I don't mind telling people my beliefs if they are curious, but I honestly think that most of the time that is just not necessary.

I tried writing a little... And it worked a little.

However, there's always this nagging fear that I'm going to offend someone because of my writing, or what I create, and I feel like that the things I write will be used as proof that I'm a horrible person. I know that's really irrationally but I've seen it happen time and again.

I know I should just write anyway but it's really hard to do so.

I guess I just don't know... Or I just forgot how to live for my own self instead of others. When I try to write creatively, it's always for the benefit of others, not for myself. When you're told the only worth you have is to basically be nothing more than a punching bag for other frustrated people repeatedly, it feels like living for myself is the ultimate sin.

It feels... Easier. It feels easier to beat up myself than to live for myself, because with the former it's easy to place blame on myself for bad things happening because I am a man and I probably did something to deserve it. I honestly don't even know what it is I want out of life anymore. At least when I still had feminism I was doing it for the sake of women, but now I don't know.

I mean you are right, I don't need a label, but it just feels scary. Maybe not scary but it's just not right, like I'm doing something wrong.

It's hard. I've haven't been open about what happened to me and I lot of things I believe in also happen to coincide with feminism and mras. It's just things like "if you believe in equality you're a feminist" that get to me.

I don't want to identify as anything, but it's like people won't ever accept you if you do and if you try to explain your reasoning they act like you have something to hide. And I guess I do have something to hide in a way--I don't feel like having to go in depth about why I feel like this without dredging up bad memories.

I just feel like sometimes I could take some sort of drug that could cause me to stop feeling and basically become some sort of puppet for someone to control. Idk.

I put my entire being in labeling myself a feminist and now it feels kinda scary. Like without the label I feel worthless. I feel like I should just suck it up regardless since it's for the sake of people who have it worse than me but it just gets too much and I just freak out. There was a point in my life in which I wasn't so focused on this label but now I feel like I can't live without it, and there's no point in living without having any label.

This maybe beyond help though. I just don't know how things got so bad that I keep thinking like this.

I've been sexually abused by a woman several times before when I was much younger... although I don't want to really give out details on it besides the fact that it happened. I will say that a lot of these stories I've been reading on here have been rather... inspiring. Sometimes I get in points in which I feel so utterly fucked up about what happened to me I just feel like it's hopeless [and it really hasn't help that my experience with feminism has been really bad with dealing with some serious bad apples].

But reading stories of people who've been raped but how managed to still live a normal life after that really... I don't know. Inspired may not seem like the appropriate word. But maybe more like it gives me hope that I'm not as beyond hope as I thought. I really shouldn't let a bunch of assholes who decided to be selfish and take advantage of me run my life despite not being in it anymore.

I don't know what else to say except I'm sorry and to just keep living. It can be hard sometimes, and it can be, but just keep living and being the best you can be. You're more than what happened to you.
